chunks: ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
I remained for eighteen nights intending to rise, but I did not get up. Should I then pray at the beginning of the night?
He said: “No. Make it up during the day, for I dislike that this be adopted as a habit.”

key_terms.أَنْوِي: I intend; referring to resolving to rise for the night prayer
key_terms.اقْضِ: make it up; perform as a missed devotional act
key_terms.الْقِيَامَ: rising at night for worship, here referring to the night prayer
key_terms.يُتَّخَذَ: be adopted or taken up regularly

ai.seo_question: If I miss getting up for the night prayer, should I pray it at the beginning of the night or make it up during the day?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on one who intends to perform the night prayer but repeatedly fails to rise for it. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that it should not be moved to the beginning of the night, but rather made up during the day, so that praying it early does not become an established habit.
